title: People Make Better Edits: Measuring the Efficacy of LLM-Generated Counterfactually Augmented Data for Harmful Language Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating sexism detection models trained on Counterfactually Augmented Data (CADs) where gender words are perturbed to flip the sexism label. The paper measures Out-of-Domain (OOD) generalization and uses Pointwise V-Information (PVI) to detect whether models rely on spurious correlations (like the mere presence of gender words) that lead to unintended false positive bias.

Analyzing hate speech detection models using Counterfactually Augmented Data (CADs) generated by LLMs to perturb identity terms. The study evaluates OOD performance and uses information-theoretic difficulty metrics (PVI scores) alongside regression analysis to determine if the models disproportionately associate specific identity terms with the 'hateful' class, thereby exacerbating false positive bias against marginalized communities.
